corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes moral from natural evil and presents Christian hope through Jesus as an existentially meaningful response, while modestly describing that response as a beginning rather than a completed theodicy. Principal limitation: Consolation and eschatological hope do not yet explain why an omnipotent, knowledgeable, good God permits severe natural and animal suffering, and the mechanism connecting Jesus to that permission question remains unspecified. Live burden: The response must show how divine solidarity, restoration, or broader goods address justification as well as endurance, while acknowledging that secular people can retain practical and interpersonal hope. Locked score: The mixed band reflects relevant distinctions, measured asserted force, and a meaningful Christian contribution, but also partial recoverability, incomplete explanation, limited responsiveness to the decisive compatibility challenge, and an overbroad contrast with allegedly hopeless atheism.

corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The reply answers every presented component by affirming practical secular hope, questioning whether divine participation explains permission, and showing why later reward need not erase or justify an earlier experience of extreme agony. Principal limitation: Its challenge leaves conceptual room for restoration to transform a person's total life without literally canceling past suffering, and it does not fully distinguish compensation, consolation, defeat of evil, and moral justification. Live burden: The secular case must explain why even transformative restoration would fail to justify avoidable suffering while preserving the difference between rejecting a theodicy and denying every relational benefit of divine solidarity. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, precise distinctions, proportionate calibration, vivid testing cases, and charitable recognition of the strongest afterlife reply, with only limited unresolved conceptual questions about transformation and compensation.
